decisive_items: isointense to gray matter on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images
diffuse homogeneous enhancement after contrast administration
normal pituitary function (TSH, free T4, free T3, prolactin)
response.rationale: The sellar/suprasellar mass with optic chiasm compression, T2 hyperintensity, and homogeneous enhancement is classic for a pituitary macroadenoma. Normal endocrine function favors a non-functioning adenoma. Craniopharyngioma typically has cysts/calcifications, meningioma is usually isointense on T2, and lymphocytic hypophysitis often presents with endocrine deficiencies and stalk thickening.

rejected.why: Craniopharyngioma often shows cystic components, calcifications, and heterogeneous enhancement, which are not described here.
Meningioma is typically isointense on T2 and may have a dural tail; the T2 hyperintensity and lack of dural attachment make it less likely.
Lymphocytic hypophysitis usually presents with pituitary stalk thickening and endocrine deficiencies; the normal hormone levels and imaging features are atypical.
